**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/08/20 (Sun) 08:41  
[USER] User identifies as a therapist with many years of counseling survivors of childhood emotional trauma.  
[USER] User's specialty is working with clients who grew up in families dominated by emotionally immature parents.  
[USER] User requests a maladaptive belief related to loving oneself.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Maladaptive Belief: "I am unlovable and unworthy of love because I was never good enough for my mother."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Example provided: A 64-year-old male raised by a narcissistic mother who criticized him and made him feel he could never meet her expectations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Journal Prompts provided:  
1. What evidence do I have that supports the belief that I am unlovable and unworthy of love?  
2. How have my past experiences with my mother shaped my perception of my worthiness of love?  
3. Are there other relationships or experiences that contradict this belief?  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Journal Entry: Reflects on childhood experiences with a narcissistic mother and identifies instances of love from friends, partners, and children that contradict the maladaptive belief.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Alternative Adaptive Belief: "I am deserving of love and capable of giving love, regardless of my mother's expectations."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Benefits of the adaptive belief: Increased self-esteem, healthier relationships, greater self-compassion, and improved overall well-being.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Unhelpful Self-Protective Behavior: Avoiding close relationships out of fear of rejection or not being good enough.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Adaptive Behavior: Actively seeking and cultivating deep, meaningful relationships while recognizing and asserting personal boundaries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Declarative Statement: "I am deserving of love and capable of giving love, regardless of my past experiences with my narcissistic mother."  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Prayer format provided:  
"Father, I repent of the belief that [insert the maladaptive belief]. Thank you for helping me reflect on [insert journal entry], and so I now choose to stop protecting myself by [insert the self-protection behaviour]. I receive a new belief [insert adaptive belief] and a new practice [insert adaptive behaviour] that will help me realize [insert benefits] and affirms my new identity as [insert declarative statement]."  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Completed Prayer:
